understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from a mind that will not settle to one quiet minute that holds the stress differently.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the unease and the phone in your hand, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the stress is a mind that has not been given one quiet minute to settle.
week_beats.steady: You hold that praise and blame come and go, and your effort is what is yours.
week_beats.act: You try giving the phone one hour of rest and the mind one quiet minute before sleep.
week_beats.story: A warrior who stood before battle and found the stillness to act shows you what one quiet minute can hold.

queries.hook: The weight of work that does not sit right, a mind that will not settle, and the phone still in hand when the day is over.
queries.diagnose: When the mind is not given one quiet minute, it runs after results it cannot hold; stress grows from a mind that has never been allowed to rest.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, success and failure, come and go; what is yours is the effort, and that is enough to stand on.

queries.story: A warrior who stood before battle and found the stillness to act, though the world around him was loud.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn, and that it feels as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna does not tell Arjuna to fight the wind. He says the mind can be trained through practice and by letting go.
verse.for_you: The phone in your hand and the four hours of calls are the wind, and the unease is the storm. You do not have to stop the wind. You can train the mind to rest, even while the calls keep coming.
verse.try_today: Notice one minute when the mind settles without you holding it.
verse.scene_line: You are on the phone with the wind, and the storm is in your chest.
asks: How do I hold the wind without losing my grip?
Can the mind rest while I am still working?

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.meaning: Two old friends meet again in old age after years of hard effort. One asks if the other found peace. The answer is no. The mind is carried on endless waves of tasks, never resting. It dances with worry, caught in a net of reckonings. It faints because it is always thinking about what was done, what is being done, and what must be done next.
verse.for_you: You have spent years proving yourself, and now your mind will not stop. It is not that you are failing at work, but that your mind is caught in a net of reckonings. The phone in your hand is just the latest wave. Let the mind faint a little.
verse.try_today: Put the phone down and sit for one minute without deciding what to do next.
verse.scene_line: You are an old man who has never found peace because the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks.
asks: What is the one task my mind will not let go of right now?
If the mind faints from endless lists, where do I let it rest?
How do I know if I am working or just caught in a net of reckonings?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
verse.translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna how to act. They are on a battlefield, facing a terrible choice about what to do. Krishna says do your work fully, but give up clinging to the results. This evenness in success and failure is yoga. It does not mean you do not care about what happens. It means you learn from both and you are not thrown off balance when things go one way or the other.
verse.for_you: The praise and blame at work come and go, but your effort is what is yours. That is the one thing you can hold on to while it hurts. The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.scene_line: You are on a battlefield of your own, and the question is what you will fight for.
asks: How do I let go of the results without letting go of my work?
What is my effort, and what is the result?
How do I stay even when the outcome is not what I want?

verse.speaker: Bhushunda
verse.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow who has watched the ages pass, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verse.sanskrit: न भूतं न भविष्यं च चिन्तयामि कदाचन । दृष्टिमालम्ब्य तिष्ठामि वर्तमानामिहात्मना ॥
verse.line: I don't brood over the past or the future. I keep my attention on now.
verse.translation: I never brood over the past or the future. I hold my attention on the present, here, with myself.
verse.why: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

prasang.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
prasang.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
prasang.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
prasang.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

verse.meaning: Bhushunda, the ancient crow who has watched the ages pass, tells Vasishtha how he lives long and well. He says he does not brood over the past or the future, but keeps his attention on now. A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
verse.for_you: The phone is still in your hand when the day is over, and the mind has never been given one quiet minute to settle. The restlessness is not a failure. It is a mind that has not learned to rest in the moment.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when your attention is fully here, and let it hold.
verse.scene_line: You are the crow on the mountain, asked how you live long and well.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.for_you: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha to move through the world with a clear mind. He says to be outwardly busy and inwardly free of agitation. Act fully in the world, but do not let it agitate you. Live fully while staying unhurried inside.
verse.for_you: The phone is in your hand for four hours, and the mind is still running. You can be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Let the work take its place without letting it own you. Your part is to act, not to carry the whole weight.
verse.try_today: Let the phone rest for one hour before you sleep.
verse.scene_line: You are busy on the outside and unhurried inside.
asks: How do I stop the phone from running my mind?
Can I be busy without feeling agitated?

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
